unit.why: A short anecdote, attributed to the rabbi of Polonne, about a rabbi's scrupulous care for tzitzit spun for their sacred purpose and the Besht recognizing that the Kalisz tzitzit were spun properly.
unit.boundary_note: 'הרב הנ׳' refers back to a figure named in a preceding division

stories.start_quote: כן שמעתי מהרב דק"ק פולנאי שהרב
stories.summary_en: The rabbi paid an old woman a gold coin to spin tzitzit without speaking, so that they would be spun for their sacred purpose; when he bought fine tzitzit from Kalisz he feared to use them, and the Besht took them, discerning that they had been spun for their sacred purpose.

quotes: היה ירא להטיל אותם בטלית שלו שמא לא טוום לשמה
tags.why: the legal requirement that tzitzit be spun for their sacred purpose (lishmah) drives the story

quotes: תן לי ואני אטיל אותם בטלית שלי
tags.why: the tallit and its tzitzit, a religious garment, are central
the Besht discerns supernaturally how the threads were spun

quotes: בורר לו אשה אחת זקינה ונותן לה תמיד
tags.why: an old woman acts in the story as the spinner

quotes: אבל היה ירא להטיל אותם בטלית שלו
tags.why: scrupulous fear of a ritual flaw
the story illustrates the rabbi's meticulous piety and the Besht's insight
the story is framed as told by the rabbi of Polonne
